newsitem.title: USA: D.C. investment executive sentenced to 41 months.
newsitem.headline: D.C. investment executive sentenced to 41 months.

text.p: The head of an investment club billed as a self-help group for African Americans and other minorities has been sentenced to 41 months imprisonment, a regulatory agency said Monday.
Robert Taylor was also sentenced to three years supervised release following his prison term on one felony count of violating court orders and one count of wire fraud.

U.S. District Judge Thomas Hogan pronounced the sentence Friday against Taylor, who has been in prison since July after he was denied bail on grounds he posed a threat to the investment community, a Securities and Exchange Commission lawyer said. He was expected to be credited for time served.

Taylor had pleaded guilty to the two counts in connection with contempt proceeding filed by the U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia, an agency lawyer said. In his plea, he admitted hundreds of violations of a court-ordered asset freeze entered on Sept. 1, 1995 in a civil action filed by the Securities and Exchange Commission against him and the Better Life Club of America Inc.

Violations included concealing more than 25 bank accounts used to make cash withdrawals and write checks for more than $325,000 and to deposit more than 200 investor checks and money orders the judged ordered turned over to a court-appointed receiver, the commission said.

The order arose from the commission's civil charges alleging the investment club and Taylor collected $48 million from low-and-middle-income investors in a Ponzi scheme. A Ponzi is a fraudulent pyramid-type scheme that involves luring investors seeking high interest-rate returns and using the funds to pay off earlier investors.
In the wire fraud plea, Taylor admitted he signed a false mortgage application in which he overstated his income and failed to reveal the commission's lawsuit against him, the regulatory agency said.
The civil case against Taylor regarding the Ponzi scheme is still pending and the Justice Department has not yet sought any criminal charges, the lawyer said.
